mission.title: localai: v3.5.0 MacOS installer is broken on Apple M series
mission.description: v3.5.0 MacOS installer is broken on Apple M series. This issue affects 8+ users.

steps.title: Identify localai troubleshoot symptoms
steps.description:
Check for the issue in your localai deployment:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n localai -l app.kubernetes.io/name=localai
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=localai -n localai --tail=100 | grep -i error
```
Look for error: ``"LocalAI" is damaged and can't be opened.``

steps.title: Review localai configuration
steps.description:
Inspect the relevant localai configuration:
```bash
kubectl get all -n localai -l app.kubernetes.io/name=localai
kubectl get configmap -n localai -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=localai
```
**LocalAI version:**

3.5.0 MacOS dmg

Apple M3 Ultra

```
% uname -a
Darwin redacted 24.6.0 Darwin Kernel Version 24.6.0: Mon Jul 14 1155 PDT 2025; root:xnu-11417.140.69~1/RELEASE_ARM64_T6031 arm64
```

The LocalAI executable provided in the v3.5.0

steps.title: Apply the fix for v3.5.0 MacOS installer is broken on Apple M series
steps.description:
## Background / the issue

Until now LocalAI's macOS artifacts shipped
- `LocalAI.dmg` and the `LocalAI.app` inside it had no Developer ID signature.
- The bare `local-ai-<tag>-darwin-arm64` server binary (the one the launcher downloads at runtime) was also unsigned.

Because of that, macOS
```yaml
% uname -a
Darwin redacted 24.6.0 Darwin Kernel Version 24.6.0: Mon Jul 14 11:30:55 PDT 2025; root:xnu-11417.140.69~1/RELEASE_ARM64_T6031 arm64
```

steps.title: Confirm v3.5.0 MacOS installer is broken on Apple M series is resolved
steps.description:
Verify the fix by checking that the original error no longer occurs:
```bash
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=localai -n localai --tail=50 --since=5m
kubectl get events -n localai --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -10
```
Confirm that ``"LocalAI" is damaged and can't be opened.`` no longer appears in logs.
